propositions: Cold-cache Pass-1 submission of all chunks and agents to a 6-wide pool causes each of the first ~6 concurrent calls to redundantly write the same system prefix, resulting in ~3.7x token overhead versus ideal.

Warm-then-fan-out pattern (proven for container bins) should be ported to the main Pass-1 pool: serialize the first chunk to completion to write the shared prefix cache, then fan out remaining calls to the pool.
Non-systemic warm-call failures must degrade gracefully to direct fan-out of the remainder, preserving review completion and baseline behavior.
With shared-prefix tokens >= CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS and >= 2 Pass-1 calls, exactly one cache write of the prefix should occur followed by N-1 cache reads across all remaining calls.
